title: Dynamic online optimization with exponentially concave losses, an unknown path budget, and single-gradient feedback.
summary: One learner must adapt simultaneously to all comparator paths without knowing their lengths. Losses are exponentially concave, and path length is Euclidean. Each round permits only a gradient at the chosen action.

model.instance: The compact convex set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$ is public and has Euclidean diameter at most $D$. Losses are $\eta$-exp-concave on $W$ and satisfy $\|\nabla f_t(w)\|_2\le G$; arbitrary admissible sequences are allowed. $$e^{-\eta f_t(\cdot)}\ \text{on }W\text{ is concave}.$$ Precisely, for each round $t$, the map $x\mapsto\exp(-\eta f_t(x))$ is concave on the feasible domain. This concerns the full action variable, with the stated norm and gradient bounds.

operations.query_signature: Submit the final action $w_t\in W$, then receive only $\nabla f_t(w_t)$. Full-function feedback and additional value or gradient evaluations at other points are unavailable. Exact Mahalanobis projection onto the public set is allowed, with arithmetic cost $C_{\mathrm{proj}}(d)$ per projection. The learner is causal and feasible. Inputs $d,T,D,G,\eta,W$ are public; comparator path budget $P_T^{(2)}$ is hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.
